summary.text: Ken Calvert, a Republican who has represented Riverside County in the U.S. House since 1992, won the November 3, 2026 election for California's newly drawn 40th Congressional District, defeating fellow Republican Rep. Young Kim according to unofficial results.
A former restaurant and real-estate small-business owner, he chairs the Defense subcommittee of the House Appropriations Committee.
Proposition 50 redistricting placed him in the same new district as Kim, and in the June 2 top-two primary he received 35% of the vote to Kim's 21%.

paragraphs.text: Calvert was born in Corona, California, on June 8, 1953, and describes himself as a lifelong resident of Riverside County. He graduated from Corona High School in 1971.
He attended Chaffey College, earning an associate degree in 1973 according to Ballotpedia, and then graduated from San Diego State University in 1975 with a bachelor's degree in economics.

As a teenager he joined the 1970 congressional campaign of former state Assemblyman Victor Veysey and later interned in Veysey's Washington, D.C., office after Veysey's 1972 re-election, according to Wikipedia.

According to his official biography, Calvert was a 17-year small-business owner in the restaurant and real estate industries, and Ballotpedia lists restaurant manager among his past jobs. Ballotpedia also says he chaired the Riverside County Republican Party.
His official biography says he has held leadership roles with local volunteer organizations including the Corona Chamber of Commerce, the Corona Rotary and the Corona-Norco Family YMCA.
Calvert lost the 1982 Republican primary for a newly drawn House seat to Riverside County Supervisor Al McCandless, according to Wikipedia.

Calvert won a new district in 1992, defeating Democrat Mark Takano by 519 votes, 46.7% to 46.4% by Ballotpedia's count, and was first elected to the U.S. House that year. His official biography describes him as one of the chamber's most senior members and the dean of the California Republican delegation.

On the House Appropriations Committee he chairs the Defense Subcommittee and also sits on the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee in the 119th Congress; Ballotpedia lists him as Defense subcommittee chair for 2023 onward.

After Proposition 50 redrew California's congressional districts in 2025, he was drawn into the 40th District with Young Kim, and the two Republican incumbents advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, with Calvert receiving 35% and Kim 21%.

He received 52.7% of the vote to Kim's 47.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News; the Associated Press declared him the winner on November 9, 2026, and Kim acknowledged the result in a statement that evening.
